title: Skyrim - Let's Play - Heart of the Mountain - Part 1
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uyU-yMW5jMg

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens a possible new series with a confession: he has been playing Skyrim since 2011 and has never finished the main quest, does not care about Stormcloaks or Imperials, and finds the dragon fights boring enough to leave the questline untouched. He treats the game as a fantasy amusement park — the dungeons are the rides, and Bleak Falls Barrow is Pirates of the Caribbean, done every playthrough because skipping it would feel wrong.

The draw here is Heart of the Mountain, a ten-dollar Creation Club release big enough to pass for DLC: fully voice acted, with new biomes including a desert and a swamp. He deliberately avoids Nexus mods, having learned he ends up tinkering with mods more than playing, so the load order stays short.

A note in the Markarth inn leads to Twisted Root Cave, a slaughtered Khajiit caravan and a collapsed portal to the old lands — a village surviving on blood sculpting, meat mines, and the distinction between wet bloods and dry bloods. There he picks up Audrey, a living doll nobody else can perceive, which he immediately clocks as Bloodborne. He plays on novice because Skyrim's combat is not good enough to reward difficulty, and rates the mod's voice acting as good as the base game's.

----

Daniel plays Skyrim on novice because higher difficulties only give enemies more health rather than new behaviour. Where do you land — is turning the difficulty down a legitimate way to play for the exploration?
